problem:
A certain company produces three types of milk: whole, skim, and lactose-free. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of milk each year:

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Whole** | **Skim** | **Lactose-free** |
| To: | **Whole** | $0.5$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| **Skim** | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.4$ |  |
| **Lactose-free** | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ |  |

For example, $30%$ of whole milk customers switch to skim milk each year, and $20%$ of lactose-free milk customers switch to whole milk.

Currently, $400\,000$ customers consume whole milk, $400\,000$ customers consume skim milk, and $200\,000$ customers consume lactose-free milk. How many customers will consume whole milk after one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

feedback.problem:
A certain company produces three types of ground coffee: fine, medium, and coarse. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of ground coffee each year:

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Fine** | **Medium** | **Coarse** |
| To: | **Fine** | $0.5$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ |
| **Medium** | $0.3$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ |  |
| **Coarse** | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ |  |

For example, $30%$ of fine ground coffee customers switch to medium ground coffee each year, and $20%$ of coarse ground coffee customers switch to fine ground coffee.

Currently, $300\,000$ customers buy fine ground coffee, $500\,000$ customers buy medium ground coffee, and $200\,000$ customers buy coarse ground coffee. How many customers will purchase fine ground coffee in one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.5 & 0.2 & 0.2 \\ 0.3 & 0.6 & 0.4 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of ground coffee is

$$
[\begin{aligned}300\,000 \\ 500\,000 \\ 200\,000\end{aligned}].
$$

Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers $(1\,000\,000),$ we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

$$
{x}_{0}=\frac{1}{1\,000\,000}[\begin{aligned}300\,000 \\ 500\,000 \\ 200\,000\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0.3 \\ 0.5 \\ 0.2\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the state vector ${x}_{1}$ after one year, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

$$
{x}_{1}=P{x}_{0}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =P{x}_{0} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.5 & 0.2 & 0.2 \\ 0.3 & 0.6 & 0.4 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.3 \\ 0.5 \\ 0.2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.29 \\ 0.47 \\ 0.24\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, after one year, $29%$ of customers will buy fine ground coffee. Computing $29%$ of $1\,000\,000,$ we obtain

$$
1\,000\,000\cdot 0.29=290\,000.
$$

Therefore, $290\,000$ customers will buy fine ground coffee in one year.
